newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on peso, U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on peso, U.S. long bond.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 30 basis points at 19.20 percent in early trade on Thursday on what dealers said was demand fueled by a strong peso and falling U.S. long bond yields.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond had rallied 9/32 to yield 6.46 percent, while benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had firmed by 2.5 centavos to trade at 7.8525/7.8550 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile down 70 basis points at 19.25 percent.
Liquidity of 1.490 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.208 billion pesos from the market during the session by placing three direct Cetes sales and two repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 90 basis points at 19.80 percent.
Liquidity of 158 million pesos was due to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank operations.
